Whereas November was first declared as National Homeless Youth Awareness Month in 2007, and every year, hundreds of thousands of American families become homeless, including more than 1.3 million children, according to Schoolhouse Connection.

And whereas there were about 1.2 million students enrolled in public school in Virginia during the 2024-2025 school year, according to the Virginia Department of Education, with about 11,206 of those students identified as experiencing homelessness.

And whereas the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act provides educational rights and services to children and youth experiencing homelessness in grades pre-K through 12, including those 21 years and younger who are found eligible for services under IDEA special education.

And whereas, as defined by the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act, youth and children experiencing homelessness are individuals who lack a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence, including those sharing the housing of other persons due to loss of housing, economic hardship, or a similar reason, are living in motels, hotels, trailer parks, or camping grounds due to the lack of alternative adequate accommodations and are living in emergency or transitional centers or are abandoned in hospitals.

And whereas the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act further defines youth and children experiencing homelessness as those who have a primary nighttime residence that is a public or private place not designated for or ordinarily used as a regular sleeping accommodation for human beings, including those who are living in cars, parks, public spaces, abandoned buildings, substandard housing, bus or train stations, or similar settings.

And whereas the population of youth experiencing homelessness also includes migratory youth, as well as unaccompanied youth who have left home for one or more nights without permission. Youth who have been kicked out of their homes are abandoned, deserted, or prevented from returning home.

And whereas Loudoun County Public Schools continues to support students experiencing homelessness and identified approximately 1,494 students experiencing homeless in the 2024-2025 school year, allowing them to receive a stable education despite the uncertainty of their living situation.

Now, therefore, be it resolved that the Loudoun County School Board formally recognizes November 2025 as National Homeless Youth Awareness Month in Loudoun County Public Schools and encourages school community support to help all youth engage in education and experience both academic and personal success.
